title: Private AI for Real Estate Brokerages & Teams | Deepvine.AI
description: A private AI knowledge system deployed in your brokerage's environment. Client and transaction data stays under your control and never trains shared models. Built for real estate brokerages and teams that treat institutional knowledge as an asset.
h1: Private AI for Real Estate Brokerages & Teams
lead: Deepvine is a private AI knowledge system that a real estate brokerage or team deploys inside its own environment, connected to the CRM, transaction management platform, document storage, email, and Slack, and backfilled with its own deal and client history. Agents and staff can ask questions in plain language and get source-cited answers drawn from the brokerage's actual records, without client or transaction information ever leaving the brokerage's control or being used to train shared models. It is built so the institutional knowledge your people accumulate becomes an asset you own, rather than something that leaks into consumer tools or walks out the door.

sections.heading: The asset nobody puts on the balance sheet
paragraphs: A brokerage's real value is not its office lease or its sign riders — it is institutional knowledge: which lenders actually close on time, how a difficult listing finally sold, what a repeat client cares about, the local pricing intuition earned over hundreds of transactions. Most of that lives in agents' heads and scattered CRM notes. When a productive agent leaves, that knowledge usually leaves too. Deepvine turns your deal history, client records, and internal conversations into a private, searchable brain that compounds for the whole brokerage instead of resetting with every departure. We explore this in depth in our guide on private AI and client confidentiality for brokerages.

sections.heading: Where your data goes when agents use "free" AI
paragraphs: When an agent pastes a client's finances, motivations, or contract terms into a consumer AI tool, that information can leave your control and, in many cases, be retained or used to improve someone else's model. Courts have signaled that consumer AI chats are not privileged or confidential, and a real estate professional's duty of confidentiality does not pause because a tool is convenient. Deepvine gives your team the productivity of AI without the exposure: it runs inside your environment, so client and transaction information never reaches an outside vendor in the first place.

sections.heading: Fiduciary duty didn't get an AI exception
paragraphs: Confidentiality, fair housing, and honest dealing are obligations agents already carry — and the legal ground underneath AI is shifting fast. Roughly twenty states now enforce comprehensive privacy laws, AI-specific statutes are live in states like Texas and California, and fair-housing rules apply no matter what tool generated the marketing copy or screened the message. A private deployment doesn't make those duties disappear, but it removes the hardest part of the analysis by keeping client information inside your brokerage instead of sending it to a third party.

sections.heading: What your team can actually do with it
paragraphs: Agents ask plain-language questions and get source-cited answers pulled from your own records: "What did we learn last time we listed in this building?", "Which of my past clients were looking for exactly this?", "How did we structure the concession on that deal that fell through and came back?" Deepvine connects to your CRM, transaction management platform, document storage, email, and Slack, backfills your history, and keeps itself current with daily diffs — so answers reflect how your brokerage actually works, not the open internet.

sections.heading: Which brokerages and teams this is built for
paragraphs: Deepvine is built for residential and commercial brokerages and for individual teams that treat their accumulated knowledge as an asset worth protecting and compounding. If your business depends on relationships, repeat clients, and local expertise — and you'd rather own that intelligence than rent it from a consumer AI vendor — a private deployment keeps the knowledge, and the client data behind it, firmly under your control.

faq.q: Does our brokerage's data ever leave our environment?
faq.a: No. Deepvine is deployed inside your brokerage's own infrastructure, and your client records, transaction files, contracts, and prompts stay there. The system connects to the tools you already use and reads your data in place; nothing is copied to a shared cloud, and your inputs are never used to train an outside model.

faq.q: Is it a problem for agents to paste client details into consumer AI tools?
faq.a: It can be. Putting a client's financial situation, motivations, or contract terms into a free consumer AI tool can send confidential information to a third party and undercut your fiduciary duty of confidentiality. A private deployment lets your team get AI answers without that information ever reaching an outside vendor.

faq.q: Can it connect to our CRM, transaction management, and email?
faq.a: Yes. Deepvine is built to connect to the systems a brokerage already runs — your CRM, transaction management platform, document storage, email, and Slack — and to read that history so answers are grounded in your own deals and files rather than the open internet.

faq.q: What happens to the knowledge base if we end the engagement?
faq.a: You keep your data and the knowledge base built on it, because both live inside your own environment. There is no vendor lock-in on your institutional memory; the intelligence your brokerage accumulated stays with your brokerage.

faq.q: Is this only for large brokerages, or do teams benefit too?
faq.a: Teams benefit as much as large brokerages. When a productive agent leaves, the relationships, deal history, and hard-won local knowledge often walk out with them. A private knowledge system captures that institutional memory so it compounds for the whole team instead of resetting.

Pricing depends on the size of your brokerage or team, the systems being connected, and the depth of historical backfill, so we scope it during the demo rather than list a single number. The engagement is structured as an ongoing managed service that includes deployment, maintenance, and updates.
